product_one_liner.value: Fly.io is a public cloud for developers to deploy and run applications and AI agents on hardware-isolated Linux virtual machines.
product_one_liner.notes: https://fly.io/ describes a public cloud running code on hardware-isolated Linux VMs; https://fly.io/about identifies developers as the audience; https://docs.fly.io/ covers deploying and running apps and AI agents.

pricing_page.notes: https://fly.io/pricing is the company’s public pricing page.

named_customers.notes: named_customers: https://fly.io/ explicitly lists Builder.io and Supabase among teams building on Fly.io, rather than as investors or partners. | named_customers.0: https://fly.io/ names Builder.io among teams building on Fly.io. | named_customers.1: https://fly.io/ names Supabase among teams building on Fly.io.

employee_band.notes: https://linkedin.com/company/flydotio reports 56 employees, which falls in the 51-100 band. A LinkedIn count may differ from official payroll headcount.

hq_location.notes: hq_city: https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/182654-47 and https://forgeglobal.com/flyio_ipo explicitly identify San Francisco as headquarters. Confidence is reduced because Craft and LinkedIn retain conflicting Chicago locations. | hq_country: https://forgeglobal.com/flyio_ipo explicitly lists the headquarters country as United States. The conflicting Chicago listings also place the company in the United States.

founded_year.notes: https://fly.io/about says the company has been building the platform since 2017. This supports 2017, although one secondary funding profile inconsistently reports 2016.

eng_blog.notes: https://fly.io/blog/operationalizing-macaroons explains Fly.io’s implemented token infrastructure, including its Go/SQLite service. https://fly.io/blog/building-clusters-with-serf discusses clustering infrastructure. Both explicitly identify Thomas Ptacek as author and provide engineering content rather than marketing or release notes.

public_docs.notes: https://docs.fly.io/ is a public developer documentation site containing guides and references for Machines, Sprites, Managed Postgres, networking and flyctl.

ai_ml_roles_open.notes: https://fly.io/jobs/index.md lists four current openings: Fullstack Engineer, Infrastructure Operations Engineer, Account Manager—Strategic Accounts, and Networking Engineer—Proxy and Corrosion. None has a qualifying AI, ML or data-science title.

model_provider.value: Anthropic and OpenAI, used for inference in internal support and operations tooling rather than to run customers’ applications.
model_provider.notes: https://fly.io/legal/sub-processors names Anthropic for log analysis, support responses and signup classification, and OpenAI for incident summaries. https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire clarifies that this is internal-tooling inference, not a fixed model backend for customer workloads.

compliance_certs.notes: compliance_certs: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire claims a completed SOC 2 Type 2 audit and offers a HIPAA BAA. HIPAA here denotes contractual compliance support, not an independent certification. ISO 27001 and PCI DSS are explicitly not held; no explicit GDPR-compliant claim was established. | compliance_certs.0: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire explicitly claims a completed SOC 2 Type 2 audit. | compliance_certs.1: https://fly.io/legal/security-questionnaire offers a HIPAA BAA through the paid Compliance Package. This establishes HIPAA support, not an independent HIPAA certification.

last_funding.notes: funding_stage: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents explicitly calls the round Series D; https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/182654-47 corroborates that classification for the latest financing identified. | funding_date: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents is dated July 24, 2026; https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/182654-47 dates the Series D to that day. The requested month format is 2026-07. | funding_amount_usd: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents announces $25 million in Series D funding. https://pitchbook.com/profiles/company/182654-47 lists the same July 2026 round as the latest financing identified. $25 million equals USD 25,000,000.

raised_18mo.notes: https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents announces the $25 million Series D on July 24, 2026, within the preceding 18 months.

hiring_sdr_ae.notes: https://fly.io/jobs/index.md lists four current openings and none is an SDR, BDR or account executive. The listed strategic account manager is excluded by the question’s definition.

launched_6mo.notes: https://fly.io/changelog/ dates “New Fly MCP” to October 23, 2026, inside the six-month window. https://fly.io/blog/feng-shui-for-robots.md describes the new server connecting agents to both Sprites and Fly.io apps, a substantive capability rather than a bug fix or UI tweak.

leadership_change_12mo.notes: The July 24, 2026 announcement at https://fly.io/news/fly-io-launches-computers-for-agents states that Scott Johnston joined as CEO and a board member, within the preceding 12 months.

crm_stack_signal.notes: crm_stack_signal: https://fly.io/legal/sub-processors explicitly identifies HubSpot for customer relationship management and Customer.io for newsletters and transactional email. | crm_stack_signal.0: https://fly.io/legal/sub-processors identifies HubSpot as its customer relationship management provider. | crm_stack_signal.1: https://fly.io/legal/sub-processors identifies Customer.io for newsletters and transactional email.
